Hey Liam — thanks for flagging this and sorry for the confusion. Calendly sometimes autodetects timezone based on browser locale or account settings; depending on how the ICS is generated, some calendar clients will reinterpret the TZ label ("SGT" vs "UTC") which causes the offset you saw.

Quick options:
- I can resend a manual .ics set explicitly for SGT (UTC+8) so your calendar shows the local slot.
- Alternatively you can re-open the Calendly link and use the small timezone selector at the top-right of the booking page (it defaults to autodetect).

I'll attach a manual invite for 2028-06-03 09:00 SGT (2028-06-03T01:00Z) — please accept if that matches. If you'd prefer a different slot, tell me the preferred local time and I will send an invite with explicit timezone metadata.

Marissa (cc'd) — FYI, this is the same account we ran into DST label parsing for last quarter; note for docs: include explicit TZ string in invite summary.

Thanks,

Perfect — thanks for confirming, Priya. I've just sent a manual calendar invite and included the timezone string in the subject line to reduce client ambiguity: 

Subject: Redwood demo — 2028-06-03 09:00 SGT (UTC+8)

Notes and workarounds we used (for internal ops and recurring issues):
- Generate manual .ics with DTSTART/DTEND values in UTC and include a VTIMEZONE block for the explicit region. Some calendar clients ignore VTIMEZONE, so also put the human-readable TZ in the subject/body.
- If a customer reports a mismatch after booking via Calendly/Chili Piper: ask them to check the small timezone dropdown on the booking page first. If they already booked, resend manual .ics with explicit TZ and ask them to delete the previous event before accepting to avoid duplicate conversions.
- As a fallback when Calendly keeps misdetecting, offer a short 15-min buffer window (e.g., 09:00 SGT + 15 mins) or propose two time options in the same email to reduce risk of overlap.
